case_summary.case_type: Contractor Dispute - Project Reassignment and Payment

contract_details.work_basis: As agreed between contractor, company and customers
contract_details.variation_requirement: Must be in writing to be enforceable

events.actor: The Waffle Co Pty Ltd & SOPE Web Technologies
events.what: Formal contractor agreement established
events.why: To establish ongoing contractor relationship
events.significance: Foundation contract governing all subsequent work arrangements

events.what: Verbal 'win the work, do the work' agreement
events.why: To establish expectations for presales work and project delivery
events.significance: Central point of dispute - SOPE denies this agreement; Cameron claims it was acknowledged

events.what: Discussion about project assignment agreement
events.why: Cameron raising concerns about agreement not being honoured
events.significance: Cameron claims Trent acknowledged agreement; SOPE denies unconditional commitment

events.actor: Cameron Stewart + Ashley Kenny + IPC Health
events.what: Collaborative engagement on IPC Health Service Directory project
events.why: To develop SharePoint-based service directory solution
events.significance: Demonstrates Cameron-SOPE relationship functioned well on concurrent projects; provides baseline for normal collaboration

events.what: SOPE recommends approval of 12-day proposal with Cameron assigned
events.why: To schedule Cameron for K-C engagement
events.significance: Establishes SOPE's intent to assign Cameron to K-C delivery work

events.what: Cameron documents pattern of unapproved work requests
events.why: To establish boundaries around approved vs. unapproved time
events.significance: Documents approval gap problem months before reassignment; shows Cameron attempted transparency

events.what: Ashley rebukes Cameron for transparency email to K-C
events.why: SOPE objected to Cameron's candor with client about approval issues
events.significance: Shows SOPE actively discouraged transparency with clients about approval gaps

events.what: K-C acknowledges project wasn't approached correctly
events.why: Response to Cameron's June 18 concerns
events.significance: Third-party (client) validation of Cameron's position; demonstrates issue was structural

events.what: ARPC project assignment discussion
events.why: Project won with Cameron's presales contribution
events.significance: Differing accounts of assignment rationale

events.what: Cameron communicates SOPE account not in good standing due to unpaid invoices
events.why: Multiple unpaid invoices from earlier projects
events.significance: Establishes financial context for Cameron's conduct; SOPE approved new work despite being in arrears

events.what: 0.5 days approved for Derwent project
events.why: Project work approval
events.significance: Cameron claims represents additional unpaid work; project blocked for two weeks

events.what: K-C work approved; availability requested for workshop
events.why: To proceed with K-C delivery phase
events.significance: SOPE approved new work despite being in arrears; Cameron relied on this approval and remained available

events.what: Kimberly-Clark project assigned to Cameron
events.why: Cameron contributed to proposal and presales work
events.significance: Later reassigned

events.what: Achieve Australia project assignment
events.why: Cameron contributed to winning the work
events.significance: Cameron claims project was cancelled then subsequently delayed

events.what: Kimberly-Clark project reassigned to another team member
events.why: Client's time constraints and the urgency to move forward
events.significance: Occurs without prior discussion; only 3 weeks after approval; Cameron had remained available

events.what: Immediate response accusing SOPE of 'despicable behaviour'
events.why: Reaction to project reassignment while account in arrears
events.significance: Shows immediate reaction not delayed escalation; relationship breakdown now explicit

events.what: Derwent Search project reassigned (effective immediately)
events.why: Multiple attempts to reach you without return communication
events.significance: Contradicts Cameron's claim of availability and responsiveness

events.what: Formal notice of breach of project assignment agreement
events.why: Repeated project reassignments despite presales contributions
events.how: Written formal notice with response deadline
events.significance: Demands reinstatement and threatens legal action; response required by Nov 25

events.what: Comprehensive rejection of breach claims and contract termination notice
events.why: To dispute Cameron's claims and terminate relationship
events.significance: Termination effective Jan 2 2026; one month notice per contract

events.what: Request to return ARPC laptop via courier
events.why: ARPC client requesting equipment return
events.significance: Evidence of client equipment still in Cameron's possession; timing during dispute escalation

events.what: Four invoices totaling $76835 submitted
events.why: To claim 'Loss of Engagement' damages
events.significance: SOPE position: Will not be paid; no written agreement; contract is for completed work not opportunity loss

events.what: Follow-up request to return ARPC laptop with deadline
events.why: No response to initial November 26 request
events.significance: Demonstrates continued communication issues during dispute

events.what: Invoice B-4155 for presales work performed in 2024
events.why: To claim payment for presales activities
events.significance: Submitted 5 days after SOPE's termination notice; timing raises questions

events.what: Rejection of Invoice B-4155
events.why: Disputed work authorization and timing
events.significance: SOPE: No agreement for work; unreasonable timing; rejects invoice entirely

events.recipient: Kimberly-Clark Supplier Code of Conduct Helpline
events.what: Formal ethics complaint against SOPE as K-C supplier
events.why: Escalation beyond SOPE dispute to client's ethics process
events.significance: Major escalation involving K-C's procurement/ethics team; could affect SOPE's relationship with K-C; reframes dispute as supplier ethics issue
